Red flour beetle (Tribolium castaneum) -- a common secondary storage pest.

Description: a small, flattened, reddish-brown beetle roughly 2.5-4 mm long, commonly found in flour, milled grain, and grain dust/debris.

Damage: feeds mainly on grain dust and already-broken or damaged kernels rather than sound whole kernels, and is a common secondary pest in storage facilities with poor sanitation or a build-up of grain dust and residue. While it causes less direct damage to intact kernels than primary pests such as the lesser grain weevil, its presence signals poor storage hygiene, and it can contaminate stored grain with excrement and shed skins (CPC 2000).
